rows.text: Build a scalable, multi-tenant, API-first customer website hosting business, controlled through Sandy Cloud and its assistant. Customers can provision websites, databases, object storage, custom domains and HTTPS, deploy content, observe usage, manage bills, make backups and recover prior releases. Sandy acts as the service operator through governed APIs and durable jobs; it is not a separate privilege path.
rows.remaining: Implement and independently verify this scope block; do not infer completion from source or registry metadata.

rows.text: **Decisions:** Google Cloud Run for containerized sites and applications; Google Cloud SQL for relational databases; Cloud Storage for files/artifacts/backups; Google Cloud DNS for authoritative managed zones; external Application Load Balancer and Certificate Manager for production custom-domain HTTPS; Sandy's existing Supabase for control-plane customer data, jobs, receipts and permissions. No Firebase Hosting and no customer-site Supabase databases in the initial design. These are design choices, not verified service enablement.
rows.remaining: Implement and independently verify this scope block; do not infer completion from source or registry metadata.

rows.text: **Out of v1 scope:** full email hosting, domain registrar accreditation, reseller registrar purchase/transfer until supported integration, generic VM/VPS and shell root access, custom white-label authoritative NS, unlimited compute/storage, guaranteed global active-active SQL writes. Sandy Mail may consume DNS automation later but operates under a separate product boundary.

rows.text: The existing Sandy API gateway is the only external operation boundary. MCP only adapts the protocol; it never owns cloud credentials. Existing shared engineering contracts SC-01 (verified actor), SC-04 (operation/result), SC-05 (effect evidence), SC-07 (delegated authority) and protected releases govern all work. Reuse canonical relations and release admission infrastructure after schema inspection; avoid parallel ledgers.

rows.text: - **Control plane:** Sandy Supabase keeps tenant/account relationships, domains, desired-state manifests, service plan entitlements, change requests, deploy job state, provider resource IDs, usage, invoice references, reconciliation results, audit and rollback artifacts. Do not store Cloud SQL passwords, Google long-lived keys or raw DNS API credentials in browser or ordinary rows.
rows.remaining: Logical create/get only; no paid provisioning, role expansion or lifecycle.

rows.text: - **Data plane:** Google Cloud handles public HTTPS requests, customer workloads, database transactions and object delivery. Hosting jobs must not depend on the customer application being healthy.
rows.remaining: Logical create/get only; no paid provisioning, role expansion or lifecycle.

rows.text: - **Provider execution:** workload-identity credentials bound to a verified operator/worker and target service account; per-action least-privilege authorization and explicit immutable release provenance. Cloud project Owner role is not a default requirement and is not to be granted as a shortcut.
rows.remaining: Logical create/get only; no paid provisioning, role expansion or lifecycle.

rows.text: **Initial preferred topology:** shared control plane with a per-tenant resource namespace, quotas, separate Cloud Run services and per-tenant Cloud SQL database/user within guarded SQL instances; separate buckets or prefix/IAM boundaries per tenant as appropriate. Shared managed SQL instances reduce cost but introduce noisy-neighbour/connection and blast-radius risks. Enforce tenant-scoped connection pools, per-database users, backups, limits and admission checks. Premium isolation tier can use dedicated SQL instances, projects, VPC networks or dedicated LBs after economics and IAM are verified.
rows.remaining: Logical create/get only; no paid provisioning, role expansion or lifecycle.

rows.text: A customer-supplied tenant ID is never sufficient authorization. Resolve authenticated identity and membership server side. Validate ownership of every target resource at dispatch, before mutation and during reconciliation. Reject cross-tenant listing, guessing of service IDs, domain takeover, stale versions and shared resource alteration. Separate environments (dev, staging, production), encryption keys, service identities and budgets. Define explicit customer deletion and export/grace policies.
rows.remaining: Logical create/get only; no paid provisioning, role expansion or lifecycle.

rows.text: Cloud SQL PostgreSQL is the v1 relational offering; database engine/version, instance sharing policy, region and HA tier are plan-specific. Provision dedicated roles and databases, use IAM database authentication where feasible, private connectivity, TLS and Secret Manager for credentials. Never expose database superuser credentials or public SQL network ingress to tenants. Limit max connections and concurrent provisioned tenants per shared instance; design instance sharding/capacity migration before hitting quotas. Test backup restore at database granularity and document point-in-time recovery eligibility/cost.
rows.remaining: Implement and independently verify this scope block; do not infer completion from source or registry metadata.

rows.text: Cloud Storage holds application objects, customer uploads, backup artifacts and deployment artifacts with distinct buckets or IAM-isolated namespaces. Short-lived signed upload/download URLs, type/size validation, retention, object versioning where purchased, lifecycle rules, deletion protection and regional/data residency controls. Storage encryption, egress and backup costs are billable inputs. No claim of end-to-end zero-knowledge encryption.

rows.section_title: 6. Domains, authoritative DNS and email safety
rows.text: **Vanity nameservers:** `ns1.sandy.chat` CNAME aliases to Google-assigned NS are **not** an acceptable delegation design. Branded NS require a supported white-label authoritative DNS arrangement or Sandy-operated authoritative nameservers and separate evaluation. Do not advertise branded NS at launch.
rows.remaining: Offline RRset diff/rollback and expiring domain challenge evidence only; durable claim uniqueness, public-suffix validation, actual authority, provider writes, zones, DNSSEC, TLS and delegation pending.

rows.section_title: 6. Domains, authoritative DNS and email safety
rows.text: Ownership challenge (TXT/appropriate provider verification) → read and snapshot existing RRsets/NS/SOA/DNSSEC state → show full diff (especially MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC and CAA) → authorised change with expected version and idempotency → provider operation → authoritative DNS readback → delegation checks against parent zone and multiple resolvers → observe propagation/TTL → report verified, partial or pending. Distinguish provider acceptance from global resolver propagation. Preserve email routing during zone migration and never overwrite unrelated records.
rows.remaining: Offline RRset diff/rollback and expiring domain challenge evidence only; durable claim uniqueness, public-suffix validation, actual authority, provider writes, zones, DNSSEC, TLS and delegation pending.

rows.section_title: 6. Domains, authoritative DNS and email safety
rows.text: Support A, AAAA, CNAME, TXT, MX, CAA, SRV, NS where supported, TTL editing, DNSSEC lifecycle and safe record deletions; validate apex CNAME constraints, CNAME coexistence, MX targets, SPF consistency, duplicate/challenge conflicts and customer-specific domain bindings. Record every old value and rollback conditions. For DNSSEC, follow DS delegation order and prevent stale-DS outages.
rows.remaining: Offline RRset diff/rollback and expiring domain challenge evidence only; durable claim uniqueness, public-suffix validation, actual authority, provider writes, zones, DNSSEC, TLS and delegation pending.

rows.section_title: 6. Domains, authoritative DNS and email safety
rows.text: Prefer global external Application Load Balancer with serverless NEGs for Cloud Run, host-based routing and Cloud Armor protections as warranted, paired with Google Certificate Manager (managed DNS authorisation or supported load-balancer validation). Confirm quota and certificate map limits; use sharding/multi-LB topology when supported limits demand it. Do not report HTTPS live until actual handshake, hostname, SAN, expiry and serving backend pass verification. Support apex and www routing with explicit redirects; preflight CAA, ownership and conflicting bindings.

rows.text: Every mutation carries versioned JSON schemas; tenant and target resolution; risk class; idempotency key; expected state version; rate/cost estimates; provider retry policy; durable job/receipt; approval or standing delegation; and a server-owned handler manifest. Return states such as REJECTED, ADMITTED, RUNNING, WAITING_ON_PROVIDER, VERIFYING, VERIFIED_SUCCESS, FAILED, and RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED; an HTTP 202 or queued job never means deployed.
rows.remaining: Logical create/get only; no paid provisioning, role expansion or lifecycle.

rows.text: Do not expose executable or verified registry flags until the actual handler is deployed and provider-level acceptance has passed. Read-only diagnostics and mutation capabilities need separate grants.
rows.remaining: Logical create/get only; no paid provisioning, role expansion or lifecycle.

rows.text: - Authenticate users with Sandy's existing identity system. Enforce tenant owner/admin/developer/billing/viewer roles and separately scoped support staff access. Maintain immutable audit references and allow revocation.
rows.remaining: Logical create/get only; no paid provisioning, role expansion or lifecycle.

rows.text: - Provisioning mutations require target-bound permission, bounded spending, quotas and per-tenant abuse limits. Dangerous domain takeover, deletion, transfer, restoration and broad infrastructure changes need distinct elevated grant/approval.
rows.remaining: Logical create/get only; no paid provisioning, role expansion or lifecycle.

rows.text: - Use Google service accounts with least privilege per project, workload identity or signed short-lived token. Do not use static JSON keys in repo/CI. Inspect actual IAM APIs, organization policies, project/host billing authority and DNS ownership before enabling.
rows.remaining: Logical create/get only; no paid provisioning, role expansion or lifecycle.

rows.text: - Keep customer build containers sandboxed; restrict network/egress and service identities; defend SSRF/metadata exfiltration, malicious upload, supply-chain compromise, crypto-mining and abuse.
rows.remaining: Logical create/get only; no paid provisioning, role expansion or lifecycle.

rows.text: - Shield public frontends with TLS, WAF/rate limits where justified, DDoS protections, log scrubbing, vulnerability patching and incident runbooks.
rows.remaining: Logical create/get only; no paid provisioning, role expansion or lifecycle.

rows.text: - Maintain separate audit for user request, policy check, admission, provider effect, independently observed state and rollback. No fabricated confirmations.
rows.remaining: Logical create/get only; no paid provisioning, role expansion or lifecycle.

rows.text: SLOs are **targets for pricing and operational validation, not current SLAs**. Proposed standard paid tier: 99.9% monthly application availability excluding stated customer code failures and exclusions; premium offers higher availability only after multi-zone service design, tests and cost modelling. Use regional Cloud Run with appropriate instance scaling, regional Cloud SQL HA on qualifying plans, Cloud DNS authoritative redundancy, health checks and monitored critical-path dependencies. Database is not globally active-active by default.
rows.remaining: Implement and independently verify this scope block; do not infer completion from source or registry metadata.

rows.text: Define and measure RPO/RTO by plan: baseline daily backups with clearly stated restore window; premium PITR/HA with documented tested restore; regular isolated restore drills. Separate infrastructure platform failure from DNS delegation error, certificate outage, code release failure and customer billing lapse. Alert on failed provisioning, certificate expiry, DNS drift, SQL saturation, quota exhaustion, 5xx rates, backup failures and uncontrolled spend. Use automatic circuit breakers and blast-radius boundaries rather than unbounded replay.
rows.remaining: Implement and independently verify this scope block; do not infer completion from source or registry metadata.

rows.text: **Proposed marketing anchors, not validated prices:** Starter USD 5/month and Plus USD 10/month, subject to real cloud unit economics, regions, billing currency, tax, payment and support costs. These cannot promise unlimited compute, Cloud SQL per-site instances, storage or bandwidth. Define clear hard/soft quotas for request CPU, memory, instance count, SQL database storage/connections, Cloud Storage GB, egress, builds, backups and domains. A free tier, if offered, must be strictly capped with abuse controls.
rows.remaining: Implement and independently verify this scope block; do not infer completion from source or registry metadata.

rows.text: Sandy records provider usage, cost allocation per tenant and service, price plan version, overage policy, taxes, invoices, trial/failed-payment lifecycle, proration, refunds, suspensions and data export before deletion. Require budgets and alert thresholds at tenant and operator levels. During provisioning estimate incremental worst-case cost and reject unsupported products/regions/quotas. Validate profitability at realistic low utilization and peak burst scenarios before launching price claims.
rows.remaining: Implement and independently verify this scope block; do not infer completion from source or registry metadata.

rows.text: Dashboard: sites and their revision/health; attach domain; DNS editor with preview and records; certificates; databases and access rotation; file/storage browser; builds/deployments, logs and rollback; usage/billing; backup/restore; team invitations and roles; audit history; support. Sandy assistant can interpret natural-language requests but must translate them into typed, policy-authorised operations and display consequences and receipts. Provide contextual setup for GoDaddy/other registrars and external DNS; avoid exposing dangerous raw cloud permissions.
